name: Can bathroom plumbing be moved in a condo or townhouse in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: Can bathroom plumbing be moved in a condo or townhouse in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: Can bathroom plumbing be moved in a condo or townhouse in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bathroom plumbing can often be relocated in a condo or townhouse, but the project is usually more restricted than in a detached house. Shared plumbing stacks, limited structural access, HOA approval requirements, and building noise or work-hour rules can all affect what is possible. In many multi-unit buildings, moving a toilet or shower far from the original plumbing chase may be impractical or not allowed because of stack alignment and building-system limitations. Access to neighboring ceilings, floors, or common areas may also be limited, which can make rerouting more complex. Homeowners should verify building rules, plumbing stack locations, and permit requirements before design work goes too far. A site evaluation is important because the best layout in a single-family remodel may not work in a shared-structure building. The key question is not just whether the fixture can move, but whether it can move within the building’s plumbing and HOA constraints.
